Title: Judges, bullying and a 'broken' complaints system | RNZ
# Judges, bullying and a 'broken' complaints system. If you're unhappy with a judge's behaviour, you can complain. Lawyers, academics and complainants say the complaints system is secretive, ineffective and broken. It was only once Laura Smith\* left town that she realised how unbearable the bullying had become. There were two judges in particular that made working as a lawyer in her small city a living hell. But what was really damaging was that you started to lose respect from other judges too, because judges talk.". Smith raised her concerns about one of the judges with a senior lawyer, who approached the judge on her behalf. She knew it would be career suicide to lay a formal complaint with the Judicial Conduct Commissioner, so it was a relief to leave town. Lawyers are reluctant to complain about a judge's behaviour because the repercussions can be huge, especially in smaller towns, she says. Judicial independence is enshrined in law for good reason, but archaic legal traditions are partly to blame for lawyers not wanting to complain, Hall says "You don't have many professions where deference is an inbuilt aspect of the job. Not in the way that a court is - and it's a real problem.". Lawyers, academics and complainants told RNZ the complaints system was secretive, ineffective and broken, and they had little confidence errant judges were being held to account. Here is how the complaints system works: No-one can make a complaint about a judge's decision - that's what the appeal process is for - but complaints about a judge's behaviour, whether in or outside the court, can be made to the Judicial Conduct Commissioner (JCC). Judicial Conduct Commissioner Alan Ritchie would not speak to RNZ, but legislation outlines the three options he can take when a complaint is lodged: Take no further action; refer the complaint to the Head of Bench (the chief judge) to deal with; or recommend the Attorney-General convenes a Judicial Conduct Panel to decide whether the judge should be removed from office. "The best way to deal with that is for the Head of Bench to sit them down and say, 'You were rude that day, what was going on?

results.content: Here’s my feedback as a frequent player and light spender. I hope the developers take this seriously: VIP Border Issue: I claimed the VIP border, but it doesn’t show up as an option to equip. Despite saying “claimed,” it’s simply not there. There’s also no in-game bug reporting or complaint feature to resolve issues like this, which is a significant oversight. Battle Pass Notification: The battle pass system is frustrating. Even after completing it, the exclamation point notification persists, seemingly trying to compel players to buy it. This tactic feels manipulative and undermines the user experience. Growth Fund Misleading: The growth fund seemed like a one-time purchase, but after all the rewards were distributed, it disappeared and became a renewal option. This wasn’t made clear [...] and became a renewal option. This wasn’t made clear upfront and feels misleading. Purchases should always be transparent about their terms. Daily Miner Spam: The daily miner sends notifications after every single mine or draw. When using the free draw option, it should allow all five draws to process smoothly without unnecessary interruptions. These issues create a frustrating experience for players. Please address them, fixing these would show you value your community and encourage helpful reviews. I’ll gladly update mine if meaningful changes are made. [...] Cute art style and I had fun with it for the first couple of days, but eventually you get tired of the UI’s sensory overload and the endless grind. It’s simple but it’s fun. However, it’s just ruined by the in app purchase spam and confusing systems that have so many different in game currencies needed to advance stats/items.
